title: Monotone Increasing Digits
statement:
Call a non-negative integer *monotone* when its decimal digits never go down as you read them from left to right: every digit is at most the digit to its right. Single-digit numbers (including `0`) are monotone.

Given a non-negative integer `n`, return the greatest monotone integer that does not exceed `n`.
notes:
## Intuition

Counting down from `n` and testing each number works, but the gap can be huge (from `989999999` the answer is `899999999`). Look at the digits instead. If they never drop, `n` itself is the answer. If some digit is bigger than the one after it, the number has to shrink at that point: lowering that digit by one makes every later position free, and the largest free tail is all `9`s. Lowering a digit may create a new drop with the digit before it, so the scan runs from right to left and carries the fix leftwards.

## Approach

1. Split `n` into an array `digits`. Set `fillFrom` to the length (nothing to fill yet).
2. Walk `i` from the last index down to `1`. When `digits[i - 1] > digits[i]`, decrease `digits[i - 1]` by one and set `fillFrom = i`.
3. Because the walk goes leftwards, `fillFrom` ends at the leftmost position that needs the fix.
4. Set every digit from `fillFrom` to the end to `9` and join the digits back into a number.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 10`, so `digits = [1, 0]` and `fillFrom = 2`. At `i = 1`, `1 > 0`, so `digits[0]` becomes `0` and `fillFrom = 1`. Filling from index 1 gives `[0, 9]`, which joins to `"09"` and converts to `9`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(d), where d is the number of digits (at most 10): two passes over the digits.
- Space: O(d) for the digit array.

## Pitfalls

- Fixing only the first drop from the left fails on `332`: lowering the second `3` creates `3 > 2` with the first one. Scanning right to left handles the chain.
- Fill with `9` from the leftmost fixed position (`fillFrom` is overwritten as the scan moves left). Filling only after the first drop found turns `332` into `229` instead of `299`.
- A leading zero can appear (`10` gives `"09"`); converting with `Number` removes it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `digits` | the decimal digits of `n`, most significant first |
| `fillFrom` | first index that becomes `9`; the length when no drop was found |
| `i` | position being compared with the digit before it |

narration.2: Break n into its decimal digits so each one can be adjusted.
narration.3: No position needs filling yet, so start past the end.
narration.4: Scan from the right so a fix can ripple to earlier digits.
narration.5: A drop: the digit before i is bigger than the digit at i.
narration.6: Lower the earlier digit by one so the prefix becomes smaller than n's.
narration.7: Everything from i onward can now be as large as possible.
narration.10: Turn every digit from the leftmost fix onwards into 9.
narration.13: Join the digits; Number drops any leading zero.
